conviction_note: Negative lean (p_up 40) on a likely second cut to the 2026 volume guide and unresolved covenant and funding disclosure, held near 50 because the stock already fell 43% in nine sessions, mostly on MSCI-forced selling and the postponement; abs_move 15 on the name's confirmed print reactions (-27.5% on H1 with a guide cut). The findings sum to -5.1 and the scaled number is -3.0: the sum counts the guide cut at full size, while p_up carries the chance of a relief rally if the release brings Geely support.
bar: Unsourced or disputed, so findings that depend on it are capped small. Q3 revenue consensus is about $847-864m (FXEmpire https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/psnyw/earnings ; Stocktwits https://stocktwits.com/symbol/PSNY/earnings ; the two disagree on EPS and look stale). FY2026 revenue consensus is $3.18B from 3 analysts (S&P Global via https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/psny/forecast/ , last updated 2026-10-09). The company gives no revenue guide, only volume: 'low to mid single digit growth' on 2025's 60,119 cars (https://electrive.com/2026/09/04/polestar-lowers-forecasts-amid-weak-half-year-figures ; https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260109689366/en/Polestar-reports-record-retail-sales-in-2025). The Q3 volume (14,371) is already public. Scaling H1 revenue per car ($1.36B over 30,423 cars, about $44.7k) to Q3 gives roughly $0.64-0.75B, about 15% under the stale consensus. That is my inference, hence print_vs_bar -15.

expectations.real_bar: The stock rises only if the release removes the existential overhang: club-loan covenants waived or amended, a dated Geely-sphere funding commitment, and no further cut to the volume guide or a cut already absorbed. A revenue beat against the stale consensus is not the bar.

next_guide.street_next_quarter: Not found as a Q4 figure. The FY2026 revenue consensus of $3.18B (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/psny/forecast/) implies H2 of about $1.82B against H1's $1.36B.
next_guide.street_full_year: Revenue $3.18B, EPS -$10.03 (S&P Global via https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/psny/forecast/, last updated 2026-10-09).
next_guide.company_current_guide: 2026 retail volume growth 'low to mid single digit' on 60,119 cars in 2025, set 2026-09-03 (https://electrive.com/2026/09/04/polestar-lowers-forecasts-amid-weak-half-year-figures). No revenue or margin guide.
next_guide.basis: Nine-month volume is 44,790 (+0.6%). Meeting a 2-5% full-year guide needs about 16,500-18,300 cars in Q4 against 15,608 in Q4 2025 and 14,371 in Q3 2026. Ex-US Q3 fell 8%, US new-car sales end with MY2026 inventory, and the Polestar 4 SUV only starts deliveries in Q4. A cut, or a guide at the bottom of the range, is the likelier outcome.

findings.finding: Arithmetic on the company's own numbers makes a second 2026 volume guide cut likely. The guide is 'low to mid single digit' growth on 60,119 cars in 2025, which needs about 61,300-63,100 cars. Nine months delivered 44,790, so Q4 would need 16,500-18,300, which is +6% to +17% on Q4 2025's 15,608. Q3 was 14,371 with ex-US down 8% (12,211), and the US contributed about 2,160 cars in Q3 from a channel that ends with MY2026 inventory.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last guide cut (2026-09-03, volume from low double digits to low-to-mid single digits) moved the stock -27.5% on the day.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is -88% from its high and a Sell consensus exists. But the FY revenue consensus of $3.18B still implies H2 revenue 34% above H1 on flat volume, so the street's numbers have not absorbed a second cut. If they had, the FY consensus would sit near $2.7-2.8B.
findings.independence: Guide and 2025 base from https://electrive.com/2026/09/04/polestar-lowers-forecasts-amid-weak-half-year-figures and https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260109689366/en/Polestar-reports-record-retail-sales-in-2025 . The CEO said Europe was 'somewhat flat' this year (https://eletric-vehicles.com/geely/polestar/polestar-has-built-first-5000-polestar-4-suvs-in-south-korea-ceo-says/). Shares the volume-release document with the reported-quarter finding.

findings.finding: The Q3 release must disclose the covenant and funding position, and the amended 2026 covenants look out of reach. The club loan carries a minimum quarterly cash of EUR400m, a debt-to-asset ratio (Q2 actual 1.47:1 against an amended cap of 1.50:1), and a reported 2026 minimum revenue of $3.30B. H1 revenue was $1.36B and even the street's FY figure is $3.18B. Cash was $888M at June 30 after H1 operating cash outflow of $850M, and only $100M of the 3 Sep $400M Geely loan is committed. A waiver or amendment, new support, or a breach has to be addressed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Going-concern language first appeared with H1 (2026-09-03, -27.5%, mixed with the guide cut). No clean reaction to a funding-only item.
findings.why_not_priced: The going-concern risk is broadly known, but the market cannot see whether the Q2-Q3 test passed or whether lenders waived it. An unresolved binary would trade like this one, with an indefinite delay and a 43% slide, and it resolves on this print. Sign: a waiver plus a committed Geely facility is a relief; a breach or a new dilutive equity raise at ~$2.8 is a further leg down. The money buys runway, not a demand ramp (Q3 volume +1%), so the lean stays negative.
findings.independence: The $3.30B revenue floor and the Chinese-loan 30,000-car H1 test, cleared by 423 cars, are from https://eletric-vehicles.com/geely/polestar/polestar-cleared-a-loan-covenant-by-423-cars-sec-filing-shows/ (snippet only; 403 on fetch). The Geely term loan with only Term A committed is in https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1884082/000110465926105064/tm2624554d1_6k.htm . Covenant arithmetic is inference from documents.

findings.finding: Polestar postponed the Q3 release two days before the 5 Nov date 'to allow more time to conclude its quarter-end closing process' and gave no date until 23 Nov. That points to judgemental items in the close, such as impairments, inventory NRV, US exit provisions or the going-concern assessment. H1 already said 'additional costs and charges may arise' on the US exit, which cost about $211M in H1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The postponement day (2026-11-05, the original print date) closed -13.6% after a +7.5% day; Polestar's 2024 delays ended in a restatement of 2021-2022 accounts.
findings.why_not_priced: The delay is priced as uncertainty, but the size of any charge is not known. An unquantified reported-quarter impairment is the kind of item that has paid before. If it were known, the release-day move would be set by the guide alone.
findings.independence: The US-exit charge and 'may arise' wording are in https://www.webull.com/news/15514532644512768 (H1 call transcript). Hurbra (https://hurbra.se/?p=50868, 2026-11-16) notes the company cited no accounting or audit problem. Related to the covenant finding, because the going-concern assessment sits in the same close.

findings.finding: The real bar has dropped. The stock fell from $4.88 (11 Nov) to $2.745 (24 Nov), -43%, mostly over 12-13 Nov on 3.5x volume after MSCI announced on 11 Nov a move from small cap to micro cap effective after the 30 Nov close. Spot ($2.78, market cap about $0.5B) is 45% below the lowest analyst target ($5), and short interest is low (1.5% of float).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print came after a forced-selling slide of this size. After the H1 crash the stock gave back about +6% the next day (baseline amc-tagged row).
findings.why_not_priced: Part of the slide is index-mechanical rather than informational (EFN/Avanza: the MSCI move 'forces some funds to sell'), so the price may hold more bad news than the release delivers. If the slide were purely informational, it would have come with a document, and none came between 11 and 13 Nov.

findings.finding: Management statements inside the quarter point to a Q4 mix and margin lift. On 6 Oct the CEO said 5,000 Polestar 4 SUVs (management's 'most profitable cars') had been built in Busan for Q4 European deliveries. On the H1 call management expected a significant drop in cash burn in H2, H2-weighted carbon-credit sales, and restructuring savings from late Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None: the stock has not yet rallied on margin commentary in the record found.
findings.why_not_priced: The street's 2026 EPS of -$10 and Sell consensus price no margin turn. A Q3 or Q4 gross margin well above Q2's -13% would be new information. The 5,000-unit build is also a working-capital use, so it partly offsets the funding read.
findings.independence: H1 call guidance on cash burn and carbon credits: https://www.webull.com/news/15514532644512768 ; IfA 2026 dealer-network push and 100k-unit target: https://www.autohaus.de/nachrichten/autohersteller/lohschellers-polestar-plan-groesser-breiter-profitabler-3918079

findings.finding: Volvo Cars swung to a Q3 2026 operating loss of SEK -3.7bn (EBIT margin -5.6%), withdrew its outlook and is cutting 2,500 jobs. It took a SEK 1.1bn negative revaluation of US CAFE credits after legislative changes and booked SEK 0.9bn of Polestar's Q2 losses. Europe and China demand is weak and US regulatory-credit value has collapsed.
findings.link: Volvo Cars is a Polestar co-founder, shareholder and lender (a $660M shareholder loan extended to 2031), builds the Polestar 3 and supplies platforms. Polestar also counts on H2-weighted carbon-credit sales, so a write-down in US credit value at its sister company may reach Polestar's own credit revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: It reported after Polestar's last statement (8 Oct), but Polestar's carbon-credit mix between the US and the EU is not disclosed, so how much passes through is unknown. This is a proxy, sized small.
findings.independence: https://borsvarlden.com/artiklar/volvo-cars-vander-till-rorelseforlust-i-tredje-kvartalet-och-drar-tillbaka-prognos (outlook withdrawn). Shares no document with the Polestar findings.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Polestar trades on the guide and funding, not on revenue versus consensus. The volume release itself moved -4.8% (2026-10-08).

findings.finding: Geely-sphere optionality. EFN reported on 31 Aug, from sources, that Geely could take a 'drastic decision' on Polestar; Geely denied any closure plan. Li Shufu controls about 60-66%, Geely took Zeekr private in 2025 at an 18.9% premium, and an Avanza strategist (16 Nov) raised a cheap buy-out by the main owners. A support or structural announcement with the release is possible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Past Geely support announcements (Dec 2025 $600M loan, debt-to-equity conversions) brought brief bounces; none came with a print in the record found.
findings.why_not_priced: Low probability inside the window and two-sided: a restructuring is negative, a take-private is positive. The price at about $0.5B market cap implies no take-out premium.

findings.finding: A 6-K of 5 Nov 2026 discloses that Polestar Performance AB filed to convert cross-border into a Dutch B.V. to make the holding structure and 'distribution of capital within the group' more efficient, with operations staying in Gothenburg. This is a structural step during the closing delay with no figures attached.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Filed on the postponement-reaction day (-13.6%), so its effect cannot be separated.
findings.why_not_priced: Barely covered; its meaning (a capital-raising or restructuring vehicle, or simple tidying) may be explained on the call.

baseline_tension: There is no skew and the baseline history is untrustworthy. The negative lean agrees with the 20d run-up (-24%) and the confirmed reaction history, but that slide was partly MSCI-forced, so the negatives are partly priced and p_up is held at 40 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Covenant finding cut from -2.5 to -1.5: 'what worked' says covenant arithmetic is inference and documents beat it; the financing question was asked and the money buys runway, not a ramp.
Revenue-vs-consensus finding cut from -1.0 to -0.6: the bar is unsourced, with two disagreeing estimate pages (rule 6).
Expectations finding cut from +2.5 to +1.5: part of the drawdown is explained by MSCI-forced selling, but rule 5 warns against reading a drawdown as overreaction.
Reaction history rebuilt from confirmed releases because baseline_history_trustworthy is false (FPI lesson).
abs_move raised from 14 to 15 for a likely guidance change (core table); p_up moved from 38 to 40 for the pessimism artefact and a partly priced setup.
